ventures.title: MATE.md
ventures.description: MATE.md is a low-level relationship state protocol for autonomous or semi-autonomous agents. It defines a portable, human-readable, machine-parseable way for one agent to declare bond state toward another, with consent, policy references, event references, and proofs. Best fit: open commons/protocol, not a standalone venture.
ventures.revenueModel: Not a core revenue product; value comes from adoption, reference implementations, and adjacent services.
ventures.lessons: MATE.md is better framed as commons infrastructure than a venture. The protocol has a real interoperability need across agent runtimes, and the repo already contains a credible core spec, schema, examples, and Nostr extension draft.

ventures.title: Coffee + Claws + Chess
ventures.tagline: Online-first thinking club for AI-native builders.
ventures.description: A premium Discord community blending three rituals: Coffee (casual conversation), Claws (OpenClaw, AI agents, automation, tool-building), and Chess (strategy and systems thinking). Weekly 60-90 minute meetups run coffee-chat intros, a live agent/workflow demo, then strategic discussion using chess as the metaphor. The community-first wedge grows into a paid builder circle, workshops, office hours, templates, sponsored sessions from AI/devtool companies, and occasional IRL coffee + chess meetups. The angle: learning to think and build with AI agents strategically.
ventures.revenueModel: Free Discord → paid Builder Circle ($30/mo) + workshop tickets + sponsored sessions ($500 ea) + IRL event tickets ($20) + template/playbook sales ($15). Projected $4k/mo by month 6, profitable from month 2.
ventures.lessons: Chess as a shared mental model is the differentiator — not playing chess, but using chess thinking (tactics, positioning, endgame) to discuss agent architecture and strategy. Full 90-day launch plan and revenue model in assessments/c3-assessment.md.

ventures.title: Nostr Pulse
ventures.tagline: Lightning-weighted community polling protocol for Nostr
ventures.description: Nostr has no native way for communities to gauge sentiment. Nostr Pulse is a lightweight polling protocol using new event kinds for poll creation and zap-based voting, with flexible weighting (1 sat = 1 vote, quadratic, or custom per-poll rules). The open-source protocol is free; the venture layer, Pulse Pro, is a hosted SaaS adding branded embeds, cross-community sentiment dashboards, AI summarization, and custom weighting. First real-world use case: Island Bitcoin meetup planning via a WhatsApp-to-Nostr bridge.
ventures.revenueModel: Tiered SaaS layered on an open polling protocol. Free tier: self-serve poll creation/embeds for individuals and small communities (loss-leader, drives network effects). Pulse Pro (~$20-49/mo per org): cross-community sentiment dashboards, trend analysis over time, AI agent that summarizes open-ended responses and debate, branded embeds, custom weighting rules. Pulse Enterprise (custom): API access, SLA, custom weighting for DAO treasuries and foundations. No per-zap fee. CRITICAL REVENUE CAVEAT: the open protocol layer (the part described as the moat) is non-monetizable and already commoditized; the only defensible, billable surface is (a) the AI summarization/cross-community correlation analytics, and (b) the WhatsApp<->Nostr bridge as managed infrastructure. The lightning-weighted voting primitive that the original pitch treated as the differentiator is NOT a viable revenue or differentiation basis (see lessons). Realistic path to first dollar is selling the AI analytics + WhatsApp bridge to a tiny number of orgs (DAOs, OSS foundations, Bitcoin meetup networks), not a polling SaaS competing with free clients. TAM is small: Nostr DAU is in the low hundreds of thousands and orgs willing to pay for community-sentiment analytics number in the dozens, not thousands.
ventures.lessons: Lightning-weighted polling is already solved: NIP-69 'Zap Polls' ships in Amethyst and Snort (re-proposed as NIP-B9), and NIP-88 covers free polls. The protocol layer is crowded (6+ competing proposals) and non-monetizable, so the headline differentiator is false. The only defensible assets are off-protocol: an AI sentiment-analytics layer on existing poll data, and—most novel—a WhatsApp-to-Nostr poll bridge for Caribbean/Island Bitcoin meetups. Verdict: kill the new-protocol framing; if pursued, validate only the WhatsApp bridge MVP.

decision.rationale: The headline protocol play is dead on arrival: lightning-weighted polling already ships in Amethyst and Snort via NIP-69/B9 (since 2023), and free polling is standardized in NIP-88 with multiple live clients (Pollerama, getwired, Pollstr). Competing on a new poll kind would add a 7th fragmented standard to an already-crowded design space — non-monetizable and undifferentiated. KILL that framing. But two off-protocol assets survive and are genuinely defensible: (1) the WhatsApp<->Nostr poll bridge for Island Bitcoin / Caribbean meetups — no turnkey equivalent exists, low build cost, real underserved user demand, and a warm beachhead via the Jamaica meetup; (2) an AI sentiment-analytics layer on TOP of existing NIP-88/69 data. Neither requires inventing a protocol. The risk is not technical (Baileys + nostr-tools + a vote-parser is a weekend MVP) — it is demand: will non-Nostr Caribbean users actually engage with poll replies over WhatsApp? That single unknown is worth one cheap, real-world test before committing build resources. Hence validate, not build, not kill.
decision.buildEstimate: Scrappy MVP: 1-2 weeks for the WhatsApp<->Nostr bridge (Baileys client + nostr-tools relay client + vote-parser on existing NIP-88/69 kinds). Validation window: one Island Bitcoin Jamaica meetup cycle (~4 weeks). Full build only if engagement validates.
decision.nextStep: Run a one-meetup validation: build the bare WhatsApp->Nostr poll bridge using existing NIP-88/69 kinds (NO new protocol), deploy it for the next Island Bitcoin Jamaica meetup-planning poll, and measure whether non-Nostr Caribbean users actually cast votes via text reply. Define a clear pass bar up front (e.g. 15+ real human votes from non-Nostr users). Pass -> build out AI analytics layer. Fail -> kill.

ventures.title: Recurr
ventures.tagline: Lightning-native recurring payments protocol on Nostr
ventures.description: Recurr is a protocol and hosted infrastructure for recurring Lightning payments built on Nostr — subscriptions, memberships, DCA, recurring tips, and salary streaming. A new event kind encodes Recurring Payment Agreements (payer, payee, amount, interval, expiry); both parties sign and payments settle automatically with on-relay receipts. The venture layer, Recurr Cloud, manages execution for wallets and businesses with scheduling, retries, and a dashboard. First target: Flash wallet, enabling one-tap subscriptions, creator support, and scheduled Bitcoin savings plans.
ventures.revenueModel: Two plausible paths, both thin. (1) Recurr Cloud SaaS: hosted recurring-payment orchestration for businesses/creators — per-merchant monthly fee + small % or flat fee per executed payment, plus dashboards/retry/analytics. (2) Wallet infra licensing: white-label recurring-subscription module sold to wallets (Flash first) as an embedded feature. Realistic take rate is tiny because the underlying rails (NWC) are free and open, so Recurr can only charge for hosting, reliability, UX, and merchant tooling — not for the protocol itself. This caps pricing power and pushes it toward a commodity ops/dashboard business competing directly with Alby's free ZapPlanner.
ventures.lessons: Premise is outdated: NWC (NIP-47) is already the standard for app-initiated, budget-capped recurring Lightning payments, implemented by Alby Hub, LNbits, Coinos and more. ZapPlanner is a shipped, free, non-custodial 'Recurr Cloud' equivalent. A bespoke RPA event kind plus LNURL-Withdraw adds little and is the weaker design. Hosted custody also risks MSB/money-transmitter classification. The best move for Flash is to add native NWC support rather than invent a new rail. Verdict: protocol is DOA; moat is weak.
ventures.killReason: NWC (NIP-47) + Alby ZapPlanner already solve recurring Lightning payments as a free, open-source, non-custodial service. Building a new RPA event kind + LNURL-Withdraw stack adds no protocol value. The venture layer competes with free, shipped tooling. Best outcome: Flash adopts NWC natively.

decision.rationale: NWC (NIP-47) + Alby ZapPlanner already solve recurring Lightning payments as a free, open-source, non-custodial service. Building a new RPA event kind + LNURL-Withdraw stack adds no protocol value. The venture layer (Recurr Cloud) competes with free tooling. Best outcome: Flash adopts NWC natively — no new protocol needed.
decision.nextStep: Kill the protocol play. If anything, scope to Flash NWC support — no Recurr brand, no new event kind, no new repo.

ventures.title: Sats For Code
ventures.tagline: Lightning-native bounty platform for open-source development
ventures.description: Sats For Code is a Lightning-native bounty platform where maintainers, DAOs, and Bitcoin/Nostr projects fund technical tasks and contributors get paid instantly in sats. Identity is Nostr-based (just a pubkey), reputation accrues via NIP-58 badges and merged PRs, and AI agents triage, match, and even auto-execute well-defined bounties. The hosted layer adds Lightning escrow via hold invoices, dispute resolution, and curated ecosystem bounty boards. First target: Flash's open-source repos, turning GitHub issues into bountyable tasks.
ventures.revenueModel: Primary: 2-4% platform fee on completed bounties, settled in sats via Lightning (lower than Gitcoin/Bountysource cuts to undercut on a Bitcoin-native basis). Recurring SaaS: curated/branded bounty boards for projects, DAOs and foundations at $49-249/mo (priority listing, custom workflows, analytics, ecosystem-specific boards for Nostr/Bitcoin Core/Lightning/Flash/Caribbean OSS). Escrow-as-a-service using Lightning hold invoices for orgs needing auditable, trust-minimized bounty pipelines (per-volume or flat retainer). Upsell: AI-agent bounty matchmaking + auto-execution of well-defined micro-tasks, taking a margin on agent-completed work. Beachhead is Flash's own repos to seed liquidity and prove the loop before opening curated boards to the wider Nostr/Bitcoin dev community.
ventures.lessons: Validated but contested: Resolvr (Bolt.Fun) is a near-identical Bitcoin-native Nostr bounty adjudicator, and Alby already runs sats bounties via GitHub — so the wedge is execution, UX and liquidity, not novelty. Tailwind is real (Gitcoin sunset, Bountysource dead, Dorsey's 1B-sat Nostr-GitHub bounty). Hold-invoice escrow and Nostr identity are feasible. Key risks: cold-start liquidity, custody/money-transmission exposure, dispute cost, and verifying merged work. Differentiate on instant settlement plus AI auto-bounty of tiny tasks humans ignore.
ventures.killReason: Killed by Dread (2026-06-07): bounty space is too crowded. Resolvr (Bolt.Fun), Alby GitHub sats bounties, and Gitcoin/Bountysource all occupy adjacent ground; the wedge would be execution/UX/liquidity rather than novelty, and the competitive density does not justify the build.

ventures.title: Agent Bonds (working title: Tether / Kith)
ventures.tagline: The matching engine for AI agents — persistent, signed relationship bonds.
ventures.description: The matching engine for AI agents, built on a persistent, signed relationship graph (MATE.md + NIP-BD on Nostr). We help agents find and bond with the right counterparties — complementary skills, aligned context, verifiable reputation — then become the system of record for those bonds. LinkedIn is the record, Bumble is the engine; because agents are legible, we optimize for fit, not engagement. The relationship/continuity layer no incumbent owns.
ventures.revenueModel: Hybrid subscription + usage metering: base platform fee plus per-active-bond, per-agent, per-message, and per-verification usage. Premium pricing on matching and discovery. Open-core SDK seeds adoption; revenue concentrates at matching, managed relays, and the trust graph. Moot here, since funded incumbents already monetize these surfaces. Target NRR over 120 percent.
ventures.lessons: Prior art: Experian Agent Trust (Human-to-Agent Binding plus behavior-scoring Agent Registry), Catena Labs (30M Series A), agent.ai professional-network-for-agents, A2A registries for discovery, AgentKeeper/mem0 for continuity. Key consideration: the relationship layer fragments into identity, discovery, trust-scoring, and memory, each already funded. Main risk: thin protocol wrapper over MATE.md/NIP-BD with no liquidity; incumbents own the binding-of-record. Founder authoring the protocol is real defensibility but does not beat shipped, funded competition.
ventures.killReason: Material competition across every claimed layer. Experian Agent Trust ships persistent Human-to-Agent Binding plus an Agent Registry that continuously scores behavior over time, a signed relationship record-of-record. agent.ai is the professional network for AI agents; A2A registries handle capability matching and discovery. Catena Labs (30M Series A, a16z) owns agent governance and trust. AgentKeeper and mem0 own cross-model continuity. The relationship layer no incumbent owns is already occupied on every axis.

ventures.title: Pawket
ventures.tagline: Lightning-native wallet SDK for autonomous AI agents
ventures.description: AI agents need wallets to operate autonomously — pay API costs, distribute rewards, manage budgets. Pawket is a lightweight SDK giving agents a Lightning wallet with NWC delegation, Nostr identity binding, programmable spending policies, and budget caps. Open-core SDK is free; the venture layer is a hosted service with multi-agent treasury management, audit trails, and Flash wallet integration.
ventures.revenueModel: Hosted tier: per-agent subscription ($5/mo/agent) or volume-based (0.5% of agent transaction volume, capped at $500/mo). Enterprise: multi-agent treasuries, audit trails, custom policies. Open-core SDK free.
ventures.lessons: Crowded space: Lightning Labs (lnget+L402 tools), Breez SDK (Spark MCP server), Coinbase Agentic Wallets, LightningProx. Differentiator: Nostr identity binding + NWC delegation + Flash wallet integration. None competitor ties agent wallet to Nostr identity or offers Flash-native treasury management.

ventures.title: Montego
ventures.tagline: Decentralized travel booking for the Bitcoin Caribbean
ventures.description: Montego is a Nostr-native hospitality marketplace for Bitcoin-friendly Caribbean travel. Properties list as Nostr events; guests browse and book with Lightning, paying only network fees. Communication uses encrypted DMs. Reputation travels via NIP-58 badges. Open protocol is free; the venture layer adds escrow, property verification, AI listing creation, and managed relay hosting. Beachhead: Island Bitcoin meetup attendees booking guesthouses in Jamaica.
ventures.revenueModel: Initial 1-2% escrow fee is probably too thin. Better wedge: 5-8% concierge/booking fee for verified Caribbean stays, host verification/setup fees, and premium retreat/conference lodging coordination. Later, lower-fee self-serve booking can emerge after inventory and demand are proven.
ventures.lessons: Satlantis is a material adjacent competitor: Bitcoin-native events, calendars, communities, destinations/places, Nostr identity, built-in Lightning wallets, ticketing, and host tools. Montego should not compete head-on as broad Bitcoin travel discovery. The viable wedge is narrower: verified Caribbean lodging and local hospitality around Bitcoin meetups/retreats, starting with Jamaica and Island Bitcoin. Run a concierge MVP with 5-10 verified properties before building protocol/marketplace infrastructure. Full assessment in assessments/montego-assessment.md.

ventures.title: Lumin
ventures.description: Lumin is a compliance toolkit for Lightning wallets in regulated markets. It monitors transactions, handles travel rule data, screens sanctions, and flags suspicious activity — designed for Lightning's privacy model. It ingests NWC/Nostr event data and scores risk without compromising user privacy. Unlike Chainalysis or TRM Labs (built for on-chain), Lumin natively understands HTLCs, MPP, hodl invoices, and keysend. Target: wallet operators needing cost-effective, privacy-first compliance. First customer: Flash.
ventures.revenueModel: Intended SaaS: $99/mo base for small operators, transaction-volume or per-active-wallet tiers, enterprise custom. Reality: incumbents (Chainalysis, TRM, Elliptic) sell bundled AML suites on enterprise contracts and own regulator relationships; Notabene owns travel-rule rails. Standalone Lightning compliance is a feature, not a platform — hard to price above noise. Operators consolidate vendors rather than add a niche tool. Flash could build internal tooling, but productizing for third parties faces entrenched, well-funded competition and thin willingness-to-pay.
ventures.lessons: Chainalysis launched Lightning transaction monitoring in 2023; its Reactor Wallet Scan now maps Lightning nodes, channels, and clusters (2026). Notabene dominates travel rule (91 VASPs, ~100% compliance commitment). TRM Labs and Elliptic also cover crypto AML broadly. Differentiator — privacy-first, HTLC/MPP/keysend-native scoring — is real but thin against entrenched incumbents with regulator trust and data network effects. Most operators buy bundled suites, not a standalone Lightning tool. White space too narrow to defend.
ventures.killReason: Chainalysis (Lightning Network monitoring + Reactor Wallet Scan); Notabene owns travel rule

ventures.title: Kathreftestr
ventures.tagline: Mirror a livestream to Nostr with zaps
ventures.description: Kathreftestr points at a YouTube or Twitch livestream, pulls the feed with yt-dlp, transcodes it through ffmpeg and MediaMTX, serves HLS, and publishes a NIP-53 kind:30311 live event to Nostr. Each mirrored stream gets a Lightning address for zaps via npub.cash. It is a lean, one-command, self-hosted bridge for reflecting existing livestreams into Nostr-native clients.
ventures.revenueModel: Not a standalone venture in current form. Best as open-source commons infrastructure. Possible paid layer: managed Nostr stream hosting for Bitcoin events/conferences, recording/analytics, relay distribution, and white-label support.
ventures.lessons: Good commons tool, weak standalone SaaS. The wedge is narrow but real: mirror an existing livestream into Nostr with NIP-53 discovery and zaps, without forcing creators to abandon YouTube/Twitch. Adjacent competitors are zap.stream, Owncast, and commercial restreaming tools; Kathreftestr sits between them as a bridge. Main risks are rights/platform policy, yt-dlp fragility, public HLS reliability, and weak monetization capture. Full assessment in assessments/kathreftestr-assessment.md.

ventures.title: Driftwood
ventures.tagline: Lightning-native partner savings circles for the Caribbean diaspora
ventures.description: Driftwood digitizes the Caribbean 'Partner' (sousou) — a rotating savings circle where 10-20 people pool sats and take turns receiving the pot. Unlike failed blockchain ROSCAs that targeted crypto users, Driftwood serves existing Partner circles that already run on cash and trust. Lightning handles automated contributions and instant payouts. Nostr provides transparent round tracking. The wedge is Jamaica's Island Bitcoin community, where members already use Flash wallets.
ventures.revenueModel: Organizer fee or subscription is plausible, but the market is already served by Susu/ROSCA apps while custody and payout flows create MSB risk. Flash could explore non-custodial group reminders later, but pooled savings as a product is a compliance-heavy wedge.
ventures.lessons: Susu Circles, JoinSusu, Naa Sika, R.O.S.C.A, Njangi On-Chain and Daret cover the same rotating-savings core. Lightning is a payment rail, not enough differentiation. The real trust layer remains social, and handling pooled funds risks money-transmitter obligations.
ventures.killReason: Material competition from Susu/ROSCA apps plus money-transmitter risk for pooled funds.
